references.text: The introduction to the chapter establishing the principle of sin committed unintentionally (בִשְׁגָגָה) and the general rules for the sin offering.
A parallel text about a person who sins by doing something forbidden by the Lord's command, even though he did not know it, and becomes guilty (וְאָשֵׁם).
Supplementary legislation concerning the sin offering for an individual from the people (נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת) who sins unintentionally.
The preceding paragraph about when a leader sins unintentionally, providing context for the rules regarding common people in verse 27.
A reference to 'the people of the land' (עַם הָאָרֶץ), describing ordinary people as opposed to leaders and priests.
A New Testament reference mentioning offerings for sins committed in ignorance (ἀγνοημάτων), corresponding to the concept of בִשְׁגָגָה in the Old Testament.
Jesus asks for forgiveness for those who do not know what they are doing, which connects to the concept of unintentional sin.
